content.title: Women's March Madness bracket live updates: Final Four predictions, schedule, TV info
content.text: March 15, 2026Updated March 16, 2026, 12:02 a.m. ETIt's almost time to go dancing.The countdown to the 2026 Women's NCAA Tournament officially began on Sunday with the selection show when the full bracket was revealed and the field of 68 teams received their March Madness seeds. UConn, UCLA, South Carolina and Texas are No. 1 seeds.The tournament officially tips off on Wednesday, March 18 with the First Four. That gives you plenty of time to fill out your March Madness bracket here.USA TODAY Sports is providing the latest bracket reveal updates, news, analysis and more throughout the day. Follow along. UConn, Vanderbilt on collision courseThe UConn Huskies and Vanderbilt Commodores are both led by sophomore sensations. UConn’s Sarah Strong and Vanderbilt’s Mikayla Blakes are both National Player of the Year candidates and their teams could meet in the Elite Eight, if the chalk holds. It won’t be an easy path to get there. UConn could face No. 8 Iowa State in the second round and a potential Sweet 16 matchup against No. 5 Maryland or No. 4 North Carolina. Vanderbilt could potentially face No. 3 Ohio State or No. 6 Notre Dame in the Sweet 16 before possibly meeting UConn in the Elite Eight. — Cydney HendersonHere’s why UConn earned No. 1 overall seed over UCLAAmanda Braun, the Women’s Basketball Selection Committee Chair, said the debate between UConn and UCLA for the No. 1 overall seed was “pretty close the whole time.” But the way UConn won throughout the season ultimately gave them the edge, Braun said.“Just two terrific teams who won a whole lot of games. Went to a committee vote,” Braun said on ESPN’s broadcast. “We watched a lot of UConn. We watched a lot of UCLA as a group. … Observable component was talked about a whole lot. The way we watched UConn win and win throughout the year, from the beginning to the end. UCLA did a lot of winning as well, but ultimately, the committee felt like observable component with UConn really gave the edge.”The Huskies went undefeated this season and had an average margin of victory of 38 points. — Cydney HendersonSouth Carolina No. 1 seed in Region 4Dawn Staley’s South Carolina Gamecocks have earned a top seed in Region 4. Here's the full Sacramento 4 bracket announced Sunday:No. 1 South Carolina vs. Southern/Samford winner (Columbia, South Carolina)No. 8 Clemson vs. No. 9 USC (Columbia, South Carolina)No. 5 Michigan State vs. No. 12 Colorado State (Norman, Okla.)No. 4 Oklahoma vs. No. 13 Idaho (Norman, Okla.)No. 6 Washington vs. No. 11 South Dakota State (Fort Worth, Texas)No. 3 TCU vs. No. 14 UC San Diego (Fort Worth, Texas)No. 7 Georgia vs. No. 10 Virginia/Arizona State (Iowa City, Iowa)No. 2 Iowa vs. No. 15 FDU (Iowa City, Iowa) Texas claims No. 3 overall seedMadison Booker and the Texas Longhorns are the No. 1 seed in Region 3 for the second consecutive year. They will face the winner of Missouri State vs. Stephen F. Austin. −Meghan L. HallHere's the full Fort Worth Regional 3 bracket:No. 1 Texas vs. No. 16 Missouri State/Stephen F. Austin winner (Austin, Texas)No. 8 Oregon vs. No. 9 Virgina Tech (Austin, Texas)No. 5 Kentucky vs. No. 12 James Madison (Morgantown, West Virginia)No. 4 West Virginia vs. No. 13 Miami (Ohio) (Morgantown, West Virginia)No. 6 Alabama vs. No. 11 Rhode Island (Louisville, Kentucky)No. 3 Louisville vs. No. 14 Vermont (Louisville, Kentucky)No. 7 NC State vs. No. 10 Tennessee (Ann Arbor, Michigan)No. 2 Michigan vs. No. 15 Holy Cross (Ann Arbor, Michigan) UCLA is the No. 2 overall seedThe UCLA Bruins received the No. 2 overall seed in the 2026 Women’s NCAA Tournament bracket and will start their March Madness journey at home against No. 16 Cal Baptist.Also included in the Sacramento 2 Region is No. 2 LSU, No. 3 Duke and No. 4 Minnesota. −Mitchell NorthamNo. 1 UCLA vs. No. 16 Cal Baptist (LA)No. 8 Oklahoma State vs. No. 9 Princeton (LA)No. 5 Ole Miss vs. No. 12 Gonzaga (Minneapolis, Minnesota)No. 4 Minnesota vs. No. 13 Green Bay (Minneapolis, Minnesota)No. 6 Baylor vs. No. 11 Nebraska / Richmond (Durham, N.C.)No. 3 Duke vs. No. 14 Charleston (Durham, N.C.)No. 7 Texas Tech vs. No. 10 Villanova (Baton Rouge, Louisiana)No. 2 LSU vs. No. 15 Jacksonville (Baton Rouge, Louisiana)UConn women's basketball gets No. 1 overall seedSarah Strong, Azzi Fudd and the reigning champion UConn Huskies earned the No. 1 overall seed in the 2026 Women’s NCAA Tournament. The Huskies enter March Madness undefeated for the 11th time in program history and are riding a 50-game win streak. UConn will face UTSA in the first round. - Cydney HendersonHere's the full Fort Worth 1 bracket:No. 1 UConn vs. No. 16 UTSA (Storrs, Conn.) No. 8 Iowa State vs. No. 9 Syracuse (Storrs, Conn.)No. 5 Maryland vs. No. 12 Murray State (Chapel Hill, NC)No. 4 North Carolina vs. No. 13 Western Illinois (Chapel Hill, NC)No. 6 Notre Dame vs. No. 11 Fairfield (Columbus, Ohio.)No. 3 Ohio State vs. No. 14 Howard (Columbus, Ohio)No. 7 Illinois vs. No. 10 Colorado State (Nashville, Tenn.)No. 2 Vanderbilt vs. No. 15 High Point (Nashville, Tenn.)Women’s Selection Sunday show beginsMarch Madness begins now. The women’s Selection Sunday show is kicking off on ESPN and the March Madness seeding for 68 teams will soon be revealed. LSU's Kim Mulkey shows off her styleStripes and sparkles are getting it done for LSU head coach Kim Mulkey, who is known for her quirky style. The Tigers will be hosting first- and second-round games in Baton Rouge, Louisiana, and are having a Selection Sunday watch party. −Heather BurnsLisa Leslie joins South Carolina watch party for Selection SundayWNBA legend Lisa Leslie, who recently worked with South Carolina's players ahead of the NCAA Tournament, joined the Gamecocks for their Selection Sunday party. − Meghan L. HallWomen's NCAA Tournament matchup we love to see: Iowa State vs. TennesseePer USA TODAY's latest bracketology projection, there's a world that exists where Iowa State could play Tennessee. In the Sacramento 2 region of the bracket, it's possible that Cyclones would play the Lady Vols. Both teams have not had the season they thought they would, making this the perfect matchup for something eyebrow raising. Will Tennessee finally end its seven-game losing streak? Will Audi Crooks have one of her annual March Madness breakout performances to push Iowa State into the next round?It's hard to say, truly, but I have a hard time betting against Crooks not dropping 30 or more points with so much on the line. If the Cyclones meet the Volunteers, may the odds be ever in Tennessee's favor. − Meghan L. HallWomen's NCAA Tournament matchup we love to see: TCU vs. Notre DameTCU and Olivia Miles will likely cross paths with a familiar foe early in the 2026 Women’s NCAA Tournament, according to USA TODAY’s latest bracketology. If the chalk holds, TCU could face off against Notre Dame in the second round, pitting Miles against her former team. Miles spent the first four seasons of her collegiate career at Notre Dame and transferred to TCU for her fifth and final year of eligibility. Miles has turned in a record year in Fort Worth, recording career-highs in points (19.6), field goal (48.7%) and free throw percentage (84.4%).Notre Dame guard Hannah Hidalgo is also having a great season with a career-best 25.2 points per game, but the Irish haven’t reached the same level of collective success since Miles’ departure. Seeing the two former teammates face off would be great television. — Cydney Henderson Women's NCAA Tournament matchup we love to see: Maryland vs. North CarolinaLet’s go back to the days of the old ACC. Maryland left the conference for the Big Ten in 2014, but the Terrapins and the North Carolina Tar Heels still have plenty of history and a second round matchup between the two teams is possible.North Carolina was unveiled on Saturday as one of the top 16 seeds, which means they’ll host games during the tournament’s opening weekend in Chapel Hill’s historic Carmichael Arena — the place where Michael Jordan and Charlotte Smith played. Before the committee unveiled the top 16 seeds, Maryland was widely expected to host, but was ultimately excluded.In all likelihood, with similar metrics, the Tar Heels will be a No. 4 seed and the Terps will be a No. 5 seed, which could create a second-round matchup soaked in nostalgia.Way back in 2006, Maryland defeated UNC in the Final Four en route to its only national championship under longtime head coach Brenda Frese. While Maryland has played former ACC foes Duke and NC State in non-conference clashes since leaving the league, it hasn’t faced the Tar Heels since losing to them in the 2014 ACC Tournament in Greensboro, North CarolinaShould the Terps and Tar Heels meet, it will be the third NCAA Tournament meeting between Frese and UNC coach Courtney Banghart. Maryland defeated Banghart’s Princeton teams twice in March Madness, in 2015 and 2018. −Mitchell NorthamPrintable Women's March Madness bracketHere's a printable NCAA women's tournament bracket with teams.Is Tennessee’s March Madness streak in danger?Will the Lady Volunteers’ streak live on? Tennessee is the only women’s basketball program to appear in every Women’s NCAA Tournament since its inception in 1982. It's the longest streak in Division I women’s basketball, but Tennessee’s late-season slump has some fans wondering if that streak is in danger. The Lady Volunteers lost seven of their last 10 games and are riding a seven-game losing streak, but USA TODAY Sports’ latest bracketology has Tennessee in the tournament as a No. 8 seed. — Cydney HendersonSouth Carolina's Dawn Staley brings in WNBA legend Lisa LeslieSouth Carolina head coach Dawn Staley recently brought in her friend WNBA legend Lisa Leslie to work the with Gamecocks' post players. According to Staley, Leslie shared knowledge with them about how to improve their game in a short period of time. The first round of the Women's NCAA Tournament starts on March 20. South Carolina is not only looking to avenge its national title loss to UConn, but to win its third championship in five seasons under Staley."There are little things you can add to your game than can impact it. That's all we want to do, is give ourselves the best opportunity to win this year," Staley said. "So everything that we do from hear on out has to help towards that goal ... [Expletive's] hard. OK? It's hard. So you gotta be ready to battle."In addition to Leslie, Staley also recently brought in Atlanta Dream head coach Karl Smesko to help with the team's 3-point shooting. Under the first-year head coach, the Dream were third in the league in made 3-pointers during the 2025 season. In 2024, Atlanta ranked 10th. - Meghan L. Hall Final bracketology from USA TODAY Sports has Nebraska as last team inUConn is projected to be the No. 1 overall seed in the final bracketology from USA TODAY Sports. Expected to join the Huskies on the one-line are UCLA, Texas and South Carolina.On the bubble, Richmond, Arizona State, Virginia and Nebraska are projected to be the last teams in the field, which means they’ll play in First Four games as 11- and 12-seeds. The first teams excluded from the field of 68 are predicted to be BYU, North Dakota State, Mississippi State and Stanford.While Nebraska lost seven of its last nine games and BYU pieced together a five-game winning streak before falling to TCU in the Big 12 Tournament, the Cornhuskers are nearly 30 spots ahead of the Cougars in NET.Richmond and Virginia are slightly worse in WAB (wins above bubble) than BYU, but about 20 spots higher in NET. Arizona State is slightly better than the Cougars in both categories. Mississippi State has a better NET than Arizona State, but the Sun Devils have the advantage in WAB over the Bulldogs. Mississippi State also finished its season on a five-game losing streak, while Arizona State won two Big 12 Tournament games, including one over a Quad 1 opponent. −Mitchell NorthamWill Arizona State make the Women's NCAA Tournament?Arizona State is on the verge of making its first Women's NCAA Tournament appearance since 2019, thanks to a strong performance in the Big 12 women’s tournament. The Sun Devils entered the conference tournament on the bubble, but secured wins over Arizona and Iowa State before falling short against West Virginia in the quarterfinal round. The Sun Devils improved to 24-10 on the season, the team’s most wins since the 2015-16 season (26). USA TODAY Sports’ bracketology now has Arizona State as one of the last four teams in. No Power 4 conference women's basketball team with 24 or more wins has been left out of March Madness. “Out of all the bubble teams, we've had the most good wins. We've won 24 games … half of those games, 12 of them are top 100 wins and we've won nine on the road. So we can win anywhere,” first-year head coach Molly Miller said. — Cydney HendersonThe No. 1 overall seed picks which region it plays inThis year, ahead of Selection Sunday the chatter has begun to build about what region, Fort Worth or Sacramento, the No. 1 overall seed for the 2026 NCAA Tournament seed will play in. Here's the answer: it's up to the program that secures the No. 1 overall seed.Per the NCAA, the top four No. 1 seeds for the tournament are placed in separate regions. Then, the team that earns the overall No.1 seed for March Madness, chooses its closest regional location.If UConn were to win the No. 1 overall seed, it would likely choose Fort Worth. If UCLA wins the No. 1 overall seed, it would potentially chose Sacramento. - Meghan L. HallWomen's basketball stars to watch in March Madness The NCAA Tournament championship is going to come down to stellar performances from the best players on the court. So here are the top 10 players in women’s basketball. The list includes: UConn’s Azzi Fudd and Sarah Strong, in addition to Texas’ Madison Booker, Vanderbilt’s Mikayla Blakes and UCLA’s Lauren Betts. ― Cydney HendersonWomen’s NCAA Tournament top 16 teams, March Madness hostsThe NCAA Women’s Tournament selection committee unveiled the top 16 seeds in this year’s March Madness on Saturday afternoon in alphabetical order. West Virginia was one of the hosting sites unveiled, marking the first time March Madness games are going to be played in Morgantown, West Virginia since 1992.Joining West Virginia in the top 16 are Duke, Iowa, LSU, Louisville, Michigan, Minnesota, North Carolina, Ohio State, Oklahoma, South Carolina, TCU, Texas, UCLA, UConn and Vanderbilt. These teams will host first- and second-round games during the opening weekend of the Women's NCAA Tournament next weekend.Actual seeding order will be released on Sunday night during the Selection Sunday show (8 p.m. ET, ESPN). ― Mitchell NorthamUCLA's Megan Grant already won big on Selection SundayUCLA's Megan Grant is a two-sport athlete. She splits her time between the Bruins' basketball and softball teams. Her two worlds collided on Selection Sunday. Grant hit a sacrifice fly with the softball team, extending their winning streak to 19 games. Later in the evening, she'll wait with her basketball teammates to find out if UCLA will earn the No. 1 overall seed in the 2026 Women's NCAA Tournament. - Meghan L.
